description: Actual isolated_stdio_v1 qualification proved the installed Docker CLI returns exact lowercase error: no such object; strict parsing only recognized capitalized forms. The source now accepts this exact additional form and still refuses transport/changed-daemon ambiguity. Initial real cat execution timed out and original inspect/rm briefly blocked despite healthy daemon info. CORRECTION to initial diagnosis: delayed inspection of that original showed StdinOnce=true and all Attach fields true already, so omission of explicit CLI attach flags is not established as its timeout cause. Explicit flags plus actual stream-contract checks now harden the source, and subsequent real terminal, lost-create/lost-terminal ACK and first-seal recovery cases passed. Original hang cause remains unknown; exact owned allocation cleanup was later confirmed and all late-created test intents reconciled with zero final finite allocations. Estimated time lost 180 seconds. Follow-up integration found an independent concrete EOF edge: the final successful input write closed stdin only on a second readiness event. Source now closes immediately; an actual OS-pipe single-event regression passes. Local timed-out Docker clients are killed/reaped and control clients read DEVNULL; a separate ambient-pipe sentinel test proves EOF isolation. These unit corrections do not explain the Docker timeout: installed dev04 from source1c29152 passed all12 unit cases but its real-alone run still timed out at Docker create15s before workload; a separate fresh create-only probe timed out after30s with no stdout/stderr. Inherited, stripped runner and SDK environments use the same executable, context, socket and daemonID with DOCKER_HOST/CONTEXT/CONFIG all absent. Earlier source real terminal/ACK/first-seal recovery positives remain valid for their exact source, but final installed real qualification is blocked on unresolved Docker control behavior. Prior dev03 late-created original was inspected with exact matching scope and removed. The two new uncertain create intents and spools remain retained; latest bounded inspect returns exact absence, which does not disprove a delayed server commit. No timeout became terminal success or permission to rerun an original.
